Rashi on Yevamot 26a:10:1.hebrew: אסור באמה ובתה ואחותה - כדמפרש טעמא לקמן, שמא לאחר שישא את אמה או את בתה, תזנה זו עמו. ובזנות קמא לא הוה מיתסר באמה ובקרובותיה, דקי"ל (לקמן יבמות דף צז.): נושאין על האנוסה ועל המפותה, דלא נאסרו קרובות אשה על האיש אא"כ קדשה לראשונה, דאישות כתיב בה וקיחה: "כי יקח איש את אשה ואת אמה" (ויקרא כ׳:י״ד). אבל משנשא את אמה ואת בתה, עומדת הנטענת הראשונה עליו בכרת, דתנן (שם): האונס והמפתה על הנשואה, חייב. וה"נ, אמאי מותרת לבניהם? ליחוש שמא עצת זמה היה ביניהם, לישא את בנו של זה ויהא זה רגיל אצלה:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:10:1.english: He is prohibited from [marrying] her mother, her daughter, and her sister - As [the Gemara] explains the reason later: lest after he marries her mother or her daughter, this [first woman] will engage in illicit relations with him. For through the first [act of] licentiousness, he did not become prohibited from [marrying] her mother or her relatives, as we hold (later, Yevamot 97a): One may marry [the relatives of] a raped woman or a seduced woman, for a woman's relatives are not prohibited to a man unless he betrothed the first [woman], because marriage and "taking" are written regarding it: "If a man takes a woman and her mother" (Leviticus 20:14). However, once he has married her mother or her daughter, the first suspected woman stands [prohibited] to him under penalty of *karet* [excision], as we learned in a Mishnah (there): One who rapes or seduces [a woman] when [her relative] is married [to him] is liable. And here too, why is she permitted to their sons? Let us suspect that perhaps there was a plot of lewdness between them, [namely,] for [her] to marry this one's son so that this one will be frequenting her [house].

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:12:1.hebrew: נשי לא אסרו - שכיבת זנות הקרובה את אשתו גמורה עליו, הילכך לא קפדא אשתו ושתקה, וחיישינן. אבל גברי דאסרי שכיבתן אהדדי — דאשה המזנה אסורה לבעלה — קפיד בעל, ורחיק האי מיניה:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:12:1.english: Women do not forbid - illicit intercourse with [her] relative [does not forbid] his full wife to him; therefore, his wife is not strict and remains silent, and we are concerned. However, [regarding] men, whose lying [with a woman] renders [them] mutually forbidden — for a woman who commits adultery is forbidden to her husband — the husband is strict, and this [other man] keeps away from him.

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:13:1.hebrew: א"ה - דבגברי לא חיישינן לזנות, שיזנה קרובו עם אשתו, לאביו של מתיר נמי תשתרי, ואמאי תני לבניהן ולאחיהן, ולא תני נמי לאביהן:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:13:1.english: If so - [meaning] that with men we are not concerned about licentiousness, that his relative would commit adultery with his wife, she should also be permitted to the father of the one who permits [her]; and why does [the Mishnah] teach "to their sons or to their brothers" and does not also teach "to their fathers"?

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:13:2.hebrew: לא מיבעיא לאביו - של מתיר, דמותרות, ולא חיישינן שמא יזנה מתיר זה עמה:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:13:2.english: It is not necessary [to mention] his father - [the father] of the one who permits [her], that they are permitted, and we are not concerned lest this one who permits [her] will commit adultery with her.

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:13:3.english: As he is embarrassed before him - [The son] is ashamed before his father, and [the father's] awe is upon him.

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:15:2.hebrew: ארבעה אחין. ולא מתייבמות - מפרש טעמא בגמ' משום זיקה, דכיון דתרוייהו זקיקן להאי ולהאי, קמא דמייבם פגע באחות זקוקתו דהויא כאשתו:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:15:2.english: Four brothers... and may not enter into levirate marriage - [The Gemara] explains the reason in the Gemara: [it is] because of the levirate bond, for since both [sisters] are bound to this [brother] and to that [brother], the first [brother] who performs levirate marriage encounters the sister of the woman bound to him, who is like his wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:16:1.english: A prohibition of forbidden relations - Such as his mother-in-law or his mother-in-law's mother.

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:16:2.hebrew: ומותר באחותה - דלאו אחות זקוקה היא, דערוה לאו קמיה רמיא לייבומי:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:16:2.english: And he is permitted to [marry] her sister - For she is not the sister of a woman bound [to him by a levirate bond], since a forbidden relative does not fall before him for levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:17:1.hebrew: איסור מצוה - רמיא קמיה מדאורייתא, הלכך אסור באחותה, דאחות זקוקה היא:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:17:1.english: A prohibition [due to] a mitzva - She falls before him [for levirate marriage] by Torah law; therefore, he is forbidden to her sister, because she is the sister of a woman bound [to him by a levirate bond].

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:19:1.hebrew: אחותה כשהיא יבמתה - אחותה של ערוה, (כשהיא יבמתה) אשת אחי בעלה, כשנופלת עמה לייבום:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:19:1.english: Her sister when she is her yevamah - The sister of the forbidden relative, (when she is her yevamah) [i.e.,] her husband's brother's wife, when she falls with her for levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:19:2.hebrew: או חולצת או מתייבמת - דלאו אחות זקוקתו היא, דערוה לא רמיא קמיה:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:19:2.english: She either performs halitzah or enters into levirate marriage - For she is not the sister of a woman bound to him [by a levirate bond], since a forbidden relative does not fall before him [for levirate marriage].

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:1:1.hebrew: ברננה - מפני רינון ולעז בני אדם, לא אמרינן ליה הוצא. ולא דמי לנטען על אשת איש, דהתם הואיל והוציאה בעלה מפני זה והלך זה ונשאה, מכוער הדבר:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:1:1.english: Due to a rumor - Because of the gossip and talk of people, we do not say to him, "Send [her] out." And this is not similar to one who is suspected regarding a married woman, for there, since her husband divorced her because of this [man] and this [man] went and married her, the matter is unseemly.

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:20:1.hebrew: יש זיקה - כלומר, חומרת זיקה לשוויי אחות זקוקתו כאחות אשתו. ובמס' נדרים (דף עד.) פליגי בה: איכא למ"ד זקוקתו כאשתו להפרת נדריה ולאסור קרובות, ואיכא למ"ד אין זיקה. ובפרקין דלעיל (יבמות דף יז:), איפליגו בה רב הונא ורב יהודה:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:20:1.english: The levirate bond is substantial - That is to say, [there is] a stringency of the levirate bond to treat the sister of his zekukah [the woman bound to him by a levirate bond] like the sister of his wife. And in Tractate Nedarim (74a) they disagree about it: there is one who says [that] his zekukah is like his wife with respect to nullifying her vows and prohibiting [her] relatives, and there is one who says [that] there is no levirate bond. And in our previous chapter (Yevamot 17b), Rav Huna and Rav Yehuda disagreed about it.

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:20:2.english: From two households - They fell [for levirate marriage] from two brothers.

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:21:1.hebrew: מיית אידך - ונפלה קמיה דהאי, ונפקא משום אחות אשתו בלא חליצה וייבום. הלכך, אמרי' להו חלוצו, דאי נמי מיית אידך אח לבתר חליצה דחד, הדר האי חולץ וחלץ לה:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:21:1.english: The other [brother] dies - And [the second sister] falls before this [remaining brother], and she is discharged because of [being] his wife's sister without ḥalitza or levirate marriage. Therefore, we say to them: "Perform ḥalitza," for even if the other brother dies after the ḥalitza of one [brother], this [remaining brother] goes back and performs ḥalitza for her [as well].

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:22:1.hebrew: תלתא נמי - מאי שנא דנקט ד' אחין? אי אמרת בשלמא יש זיקה, אשמעי' רבותא, דאע"ג דתרי אחי נינהו, ולא אלימא זיקתו דקמא דמייבם, דמצינו למימר: ההיא רמיא קמיה, ואחותה קמי' אחיו — ואפ"ה אסור; וכ"ש שלשה אחין, ב' מהם נשואים שתי אחיות ומתו, ונפלו שתיהן לפני זה, שתיהן אסורות, דתרוייהו עליה רמיא וזיקתו חמורה, וכי נסיב הוי פגע באחות זקוקתו. אלא אי משום ביטול מצות יבמין, אפי' תלתא נמי, ומתו השנים הנשואים שתי אחית — שתיהן חולצות, דאי מייבם חדא, נפקא אידך בולא כלום:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:22:1.english: Three [brothers] as well - Why did [the Mishnah] specifically mention four brothers? Granted, if you say there is *zikah* [a levirate bond], it teaches us a novel point: that even though there are two [surviving] brothers, and the *zikah* of the first one who performs levirate marriage is not strong — since we can say that this one is cast before him and her sister is before his brother — even so, it is forbidden; and all the more so [in the case of] three brothers, two of whom are married to two sisters and died, and both [widows] fell before this [remaining brother], [that] both of them are forbidden, since both are cast upon him and his *zikah* is severe, and when he marries [one], he encounters the sister of his *zekukah* [woman bound to him by levirate bond]. Rather, if [the prohibition is] because of nullification of the mitzvah of levirate marriage, even [with] three [brothers] as well, when the two married to two sisters died — both perform *chalitzah*, for if he performs levirate marriage with one, the other leaves with nothing.

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:2:1.hebrew: וכולם - החכם, והמביא גט, והמעיד באשה להשיאה, דתנן בהן לא יכנוס:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:2:1.english: And all of them - The sage, the one who brings a bill of divorce, and the one who testifies regarding a woman to permit her to marry, concerning whom we learned in the Mishnah: "He may not marry [her]."

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:2:2.hebrew: שהיו להם נשים - בשעת מעשה ומתו לאחר זמן, מותרות אלו לינשא להם. דהשתא ליכא חשד, שהרי בשעה שהעיד בה העד או שאסרה חכם היתה אשתו קיימת, ולא לישא את זו נתכוין:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:2:2.english: [That] they had wives - at the time of the act, and [their wives] died after some time, these [women] are permitted to marry them. For now there is no suspicion, since at the time that the witness testified regarding her or that a sage forbade her [to her husband], his wife was alive, and he did not intend to marry this [woman].

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:3:1.english: And all of them - These women.

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:3:2.hebrew: שנישאו - לאחרים, כשאסרה חכם או כשהעיד עד במיתת בעלה, ומתו הבעלים השניים:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:3:2.english: Who were married - to others, when a sage forbade her [to her husband] or when a witness testified regarding her husband's death, and the second husbands died.

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:3:3.english: [They are] permitted to be married - To the sage, to the witness, or to the one who brings a bill of divorce.

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:3:4.hebrew: וכולן - הנשים האלו מותרות לבניהם או לאחיהם של אלו המתירים אותן, ואין אסורות אלא להן לבדן:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:3:4.english: And all of them - These women are permitted to the sons or to the brothers of those who permitted them [to remarry], and they are prohibited only to them alone.

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:4:1.hebrew: נתגרשו לא - דע"י שנתן את עיניו בזו שהתיר, גירש את אשתו:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:4:1.english: [If they] were divorced, no - Because by setting his eyes on this [woman] whom he rendered permitted, he divorced his wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:5:1.hebrew: הא - דקתני אפי' נתגרשו, כגון דהוי להו קטטה מקמי הכי, דעדיין לא נתן דעתו על זאת:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:5:1.english: This [case] - where it teaches "even if they were divorced," [refers to a case] such as when there was a quarrel between them prior to this, [so] that he had not yet set his mind upon this [woman].

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:6:1.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr>: ואיבעית אימא אידי ואידי דלא הוו להו קטטה:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:6:1.english: We read [the text]: "And if you wish, say: Both this and that [were said in cases] when they had no quarrel."

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:6:2.hebrew: הא - דקתני נתגרשו לא, בדארגיל הוא קטטה, שהוא התחיל להקניט את אשתו:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:6:2.english: This - where it teaches [that if] they were divorced [he may] not [marry her], [is] when he started a quarrel, meaning that he began to provoke his wife.

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:6:3.hebrew: והא - דקתני אפי' נתגרשו, בדארגילה היא קטטה, שהיא הקניטתו תחלה:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:6:3.english: And that - Where [the baraita] teaches [that] even [if] they were divorced, [it is] when she started a quarrel, [meaning] that she provoked him first.

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:7:1.hebrew: קס"ד מיתה אמיתה - הא דקתני "וכולן שנישאו לאחרים ומתו", קאי נמי ארישא דקתני "מת, הרגתיו, הרגנוהו — לא ישא את אשתו". וקתני דאם נישאת לאחר על פיו ומת השני הזה, מותרת לינשא לעד זה; ואע"פ שמתו ב' בעליה, תנשא לשלישי, ולא אמרינן הוחזקה זו קטלנית שהנושאה מת. וגירושין דקתני "נתגרשה", קאי אגירושין דלעיל "המביא גט כו'", ואשמעינן דאם נשאת לאחר באותו הגט וגירשה השני הזה, מותרת לינשא למביא גיטה הראשון:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:7:1.english: It enters our mind [to say] death after death - That which [the Mishnah] teaches, "And all of them who married others and died," refers also to the first clause, which teaches: "[If he testified that her husband] died, [or] 'I killed him,' [or] 'We killed him,' he may not marry his wife." And it teaches that if she married another [man] based on his testimony and this second [husband] died, she is permitted to marry this witness; even though two of her husbands have died, she may marry a third, and we do not say [that] she has become established as a lethal woman, [such] that whoever marries her dies. And "divorce," where it teaches "she was divorced," refers to the divorce [mentioned] above, "One who brings a bill of divorce, etc.," and it teaches us that if she married another [man] on the basis of that bill of divorce and this second [husband] divorced her, she is permitted to marry the one who brought her first bill of divorce.

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:8:1.hebrew: בתרי זימני הויא חזקה - לקמן בהבא על יבמתו (יבמות דף סד:): ניסת לראשון ומת, לשני ומת, לשלישי לא תינשא, דברי רבי. ומתני' דלא כרבי, דאי רבי, נהי דחשד ליכא, מיהו לכל העולם אסורה, שהוחזקה להתאלמן או להתגרש:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:8:1.english: After two times there is a presumption - Later, in [the chapter] Haba al Yevimto (Yevamot 64b): [If a woman] married a first [husband] and he died, [and] a second [husband] and he died, she may not marry a third [husband]; [these are] the words of Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi]. And our Mishnah is not in accordance with Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], for if [it were in accordance with] Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], granted that there is no suspicion [of collusion], nevertheless she would be forbidden to everyone [else], since she has established a presumption of being widowed or divorced.

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:9:1.hebrew: מיתה - דקתני הכא שנישאו לאחרים ומתו מותרות, לאו אכולהו דלעיל קאי, אלא אגירושין ואמביא גט או חכם שאסר את האשה:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:9:1.english: Death - That [which the Mishnah] teaches here, "they married others and died, they are permitted," does not refer to all of those [cases] above, but rather to divorce, and to one who brings a bill of divorce, or a sage who forbade the woman [to her husband].

Rashi on Yevamot 26a:9:2.hebrew: וגירושין - דהכא אמת, הרגתיו, הרגנוהו, ומש"ה כשנתגרשה משני זה מותרת לשלישי, שעדיין לא הוחזקה בחדא ריעותא תרי זימני:
Rashi on Yevamot 26a:9:2.english: And divorce - [The reference] here is to [the cases of] "he died," "I killed him," [or] "we killed him," and therefore when she was divorced from this second [husband], she is permitted to a third [husband], for she has not yet been established [with] one [and the same] negative presumption twice.

Tosafot on Yevamot 26a:13:1.hebrew: אי הכי אביו נמי - לא מצי לשנויי דנקט בנו לרבותא, אע"ג דאסור באנוסת אביו לר' יהודה; דהתינח "בניהן", אבל "אחיהן" אמאי נקט, אי לאו לדקדק "אבל לאביו לא":
Tosafot on Yevamot 26a:13:1.english: "If so, his father as well" - [The Gemara] could not answer that [the Mishnah] stated "his son" as a novelty, even though [a son] is forbidden to a woman violated by his father according to Rabbi Yehudah; for that would be well and good [regarding] "their sons," but why did it state "their brothers," if not to imply "but not to his father"?

Tosafot on Yevamot 26a:15:1.hebrew: חולצות ולא מתייבמות - פירשתי לעיל (יבמות דף יח. ד"ה דלמא וכו'), ועוד נפרש בגמ' גבי פלוגתא דרב ור' יוחנן:
Tosafot on Yevamot 26a:15:1.english: "They perform ḥalitza and may not enter into levirate marriage" - I explained above (Yevamot 18a, s.v. dilma, etc.), and we will explain further in the Gemara regarding the dispute between Rav and Rabbi Yochanan.

Tosafot on Yevamot 26a:22:1.hebrew: אי הכי תלתא נמי - אי אמרת בשלמא יש זיקה, ניחא דנקט ארבעה לאשמועינן דאפי' בתרי יש זיקה. אלא אי אין זיקה, וטעמא משום ביטול מצות יבמין, לישמעינן תלתא דהוי רבותא טפי — דאסור לבטל אע"ג דחדא מינייהו לא חזיא לייבומי, וכל שכן בד' דשתיהן ראויות להתייבם, זה אחת וזה אחת, דאסור. ועוד אר"י, דמצי לפרש דס"ד השתא דחיישינן למיתה דתרי כמו למיתה דחד, ולהכי פריך: "א"ה תלתא נמי?" כיון דלא אתא לאשמועינן חידוש של חשש מיתה — מדלא נקט חמשה דהוי רבותא טפי — אלא לאשמעינן דאסור לבטל, זה יכול להשמיענו אפילו בתלתא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 26a:22:1.english: "If so, three as well?" - Granted, if you say there is zikah [a levirate bond], it is understandable that [the Mishnah] chose [the case of] four [brothers] to teach us that even with two [surviving brothers] there is zikah. But if there is no zikah, and the reason is because of negating the mitzvah of yevamim [levirate brothers], let it teach us [the case of] three [brothers], which would be a greater novelty — that it is forbidden to negate [the mitzvah] even though one of them is not fit for yibum, and all the more so in [the case of] four [brothers], where both of them are fit for yibum, this [brother] one [widow] and that [brother] one [widow], that it is forbidden. And furthermore, Rabbi Yitzchak says that one can explain that we currently assume [the Gemara] is concerned about the death of two [brothers] just as [it is concerned] about the death of one, and therefore it asks: "If so, three as well?" Since [the Mishnah] did not come to teach us a novelty regarding the concern of death — given that it did not choose [the case of] five [brothers], which would be a greater novelty — rather, [it came] to teach us that it is forbidden to negate [the mitzvah], this it could teach us even with three [brothers].

Tosafot on Yevamot 26a:9:1.hebrew: אגירושין - אגב מיתה נקט גירושין, דאפי' נתגרשה כמה פעמים שריא לינשא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 26a:9:1.english: Regarding divorce - It mentions divorce incidentally alongside death, for even if she was divorced several times, she is permitted to marry.
